speaker_role: former admissions officer (former admissions officer, University of Chicago; now college counselor at InGenius Prep)
commercial_incentive: yes - InGenius Prep is a paid admissions consulting company and repeatedly promotes free strategy calls and its counseling program
key_insights: Strong CS applicants need more than math/coding excellence; involvement in the humanities/liberal arts side and clear personal interests helps them stand out since top testing and grades are already assumed for the applicant pool.
Recommended academic benchmark is reaching AP Calculus BC by graduation, ideally continuing to multivariable calculus or linear algebra.

Recommended summer programs include Stanford and Carnegie Mellon for pure CS, and interdisciplinary options like University of Chicago (data science/public policy) and Carleton College (game design, machine learning).

Competitions to consider: USACO (US), CCC (Canada), and Kaggle for data science; hackathons and open-source contribution are also strongly recommended, including students starting their own hackathon as a signature project.
There are no true 'safety schools' for CS/engineering; the speaker mentally raises the selectivity tier by at least one level whenever CS/engineering is involved.
Common application mistakes: opening an essay with 'I've loved computer science since I was three,' having no interests outside CS, and not researching why a specific program/school fits the student.
Personal statements should focus on the 'why' behind a project or interest (purpose, values) rather than simply listing accomplishments already shown in the activities list.
For remote/COVID-affected years, admissions officers look for evidence of how students pivoted, and there is a dedicated application section to explain pandemic impact.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Recommends reaching AP Calculus BC (or higher, e.g., multivariable calc/linear algebra) by senior year, per the former UChicago admissions officer
Rising seniors still have until November (early) or January (regular) deadlines to develop one strong signature project, per the speaker
notable_or_distinctive: Gives concrete named examples of interdisciplinary CS project outcomes from real advisees (a dual CS/history major who built a video game about the Byzantine Empire), illustrating the 'combine CS with any interest' advice with a specific case.
reliability_notes: Speaker has genuine former-admissions-officer credentials at a specific institution, but advice reflects her own consulting practice's experience with a self-selected client population and is delivered inside a sales-oriented podcast for a paid consulting firm.
